title: Choose the visual world for GoalieIQ
question: The roll assigned Custom Pads. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Custom Pads
options.lineage: custom goalie leg-pad graphics: angled colour panels, quilted channels, stitched wordmarks
options.thesis: GoalieIQ cut and stitched like a goalie's own custom pads.
materials: white PU face with vertical quilted channels
options.viewport: Your save photo edge to edge; a heavy condensed-italic headline across its lower third, a tag label pinned to the puck, and a start-free email field; the photo ends at an angled pad seam into the green panel.
options.risk: Pushed too far it turns into a gear costume; panels and stitching must do structural work, not decorate.

raised.raise: Shot results are drawn by stitch, not colour alone: solid stitch for a save, broken stitch for a goal, everywhere a shot appears.
Every headline number unpicks to its shots: a stat opens down to the tagged shots and clips that made it.
The hero photo gets the whole viewport and quiet: one headline, one field, nothing else on the ice.
One type family at five width steps carries the whole hierarchy, from pad-wordmark italic to table digits.

options.label: Telestrator Replay
options.lineage: Hockey Night in Canada replay telestrator and broadcast stat packages
options.thesis: Every page is a paused replay with the analyst's marker on it.
options.viewport: Your save photo as a paused replay, telestrator circle on the puck and an arrow to the glove, the headline in a lower-third bar with the start field.
options.risk: Familiar: this is where most sports-analytics pages land, and the TV-graphics look dates fast.

options.label: Shot Event Display
options.thesis: A game drawn as one event: every shot a track curving into the crease rings.
options.viewport: Photo first, then the page drops into a full-width ring section where a sample game's shots arc in, goals as red bars stacked at the net.
options.case: Carries the shot-level mechanism vividly; loses on identification, since it reads as a physics lab, not a rink.
options.risk: Dark glowing data on black is close to the neon-on-black look the brief wants to avoid.

options.label: Fashion Flagship
options.thesis: Slow full-bleed looks framed by vast space.
options.viewport: The save photo alone with one enormous word.
options.case: Fits the photo, but hides the data goalies and coaches come for.
options.kept: The photo owns the viewport with nothing else on the ice.
options.risk: Pretty and empty for an analytics product.

options.label: Jackfield Schedule
options.thesis: Numbered amber lanes where every state is drawn by line pattern.
options.case: Nothing in it says hockey to a goalie or a parent.
options.kept: State drawn by stroke pattern instead of colour.

options.label: Jacquard Brocade
options.thesis: A finished pattern traceable to every thread decision.
options.viewport: A woven motif over its instruction rows.
options.case: Beautiful, but the audience has no connection to looms.
options.kept: Traceability from the finished picture down to each decision.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.thesis: One face at many sizes as the whole page.
options.viewport: A pixel headline over dense columns.
options.case: No hockey in it, and pixel type fights the photo.
options.kept: One family carries every level of hierarchy.

options.label: Rain Night City
options.thesis: Synchronized night bands of skyline, street and reflection.
options.viewport: A skyline band over its own reflection.
options.case: Mood without mechanism; nothing to do with the rink.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A sports-analytics SaaS page, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Photo hero with headline and button, then a dashboard screenshot and feature rows.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other stats app, which is what the brief asked to avoid.
